To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the roughness of the interface between the substrate and the first deposited layer is the most important factor in the determination of the optical properties of the multilayer coatings, and that the correlation between the roughnesses at adjacent interfaces is the main parameter that determines the optical performance of the coatings.

the interfacial rms roughness of multilayer coatings increases with the number of layers, that it depends on the substrate material, that the rms roughness is correlated over a length scale that increases with the number N of deposited layers, and that the scattering properties are well reproduced by a model that includes the statistical correlation of the interfacial roughenss.
(1) the rms roughness of the interfaces increases linearly with the coating thickness and that (2) the correlation length of the roughness is of the order of the wavelength of light, i.e., 193 nm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of optical thin film materials for the fabrication of optical elements for 193 nm lithography.
the development of high-reflectance, broadband coatings for 193-nm excimer lasers.
the characterization of ion-beam-sputtered fluoride coatings for 157 and 193 nm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given coating thickness, there is no significant difference between the roughness of the interfaces of ion-beam-sputtered and magnetron-sputtered coatings.
the interfacial roughens are correlated and that the correlation length increases with coating thickness.
the scattering characteristics of the fluoride coatings can be explained by the interfacial roughening, which is caused by the ion bombardment during the coating process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ion beam sputtered fluoride coatings are suitable candidates for high-reflectivity optics in the 193-nm spectral region, provided that their interfaces are sufficiently smooth and that the roughnesses of adjacent interfaces are uncorrelated.
the interfacial roughening is not a simple linear process and that it is necessary to take into account a correlation of the roughnesses of the different layers.
the measured scattering is well described by the theory of rough surfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given coating design, the roughness of the interface between the substrate and the first layer of the stack is a key factor in the overall scattering performance.
, for the investigated systems, the interfacial roughening is not a simple self-affine process.
the interfacial roughening process is strongly influenced by the nature of the substrate, and that the interfacially roughened layers are not necessarily correlated.
